text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Iraqi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Revolutionary Command Council issues decree pardoning Kurds of previous offences; the decree does cover spies as well as people accused of rape and looting of state property.
- Iraq holds talks with U.N. Security Council members on sanctions.
- Tunisia calls on Ankara to stop interfering in Iraq's internal affairs.
- Iraqi delegation continues meetings in Ankara on Turkey's plans to set up security zone in northern Iraq.
- (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat says Iraq is defending its sovereignty.
- Delegation of Jordanian MPs to go to Ankara to inform Turkey of risks involved in its decision to create security cordon in northern Iraq.
- Planes of the American enemy continue violation of Iraqi territory.
- Ministry of Interior takes steps to implement President Saddam Hussein's decision to remove internal blockade on Kurds.
- Great numbers of Kurds flock to government-controlled areas.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ)
- Editorial says Clinton has no more options at his disposal for threatening Iraq.
- (Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin) Erbakan receives Iraqi delegation.
BABEL (Newspaper of Saddam's eldest son Uday)
- Editorial lambasts Turkey for its plan to create buffer zone in northern Iraq.
